question: What two core dimensions combine to make up the complete practice of nursing?
explanation: Nursing requires both the empirical evidence of science and the compassionate human interaction of art to care for patients effectively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is the 'art' of nursing just as important as the science when caring for patients?

options.A: It helps patients feel valued and understood during stressful health crises
options.B: It replaces the need to administer complex pharmacological treatments
options.C: It allows nurses to diagnose medical diseases without a doctor
options.D: It guarantees that hospital financial records balance at month end

explanation: You've got this! Nursing isn't just about medications and procedures. The 'art' is your empathy and communication, which help patients feel safe and cared for when they are scared and sick. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: Whose famous definition of nursing focused on putting the patient in the best condition for nature to act?
explanation: Think back to the mother of modern nursing! Florence Nightingale believed that fresh air, clean water, and quiet surroundings help the patient's body heal itself. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: Virginia Henderson's classic definition of nursing centers around helping patients achieve what main goal?

options.D: Achieving independence in basic daily activities

explanation: Henderson saw the nurse's main job as helping patients do things for themselves as soon as they are able, focusing on basic human needs like breathing, eating, and moving. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: The opening of which hospital by Florence Nightingale marked the start of modern professional nursing training?
explanation: Florence Nightingale set up her very first formal training school for nurses at St Thomas' Hospital in London back in 1860. Great landmark to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: What was nursing care mostly like before formal training schools were established?

options.A: Custodial care based on domestic or religious traditions
options.B: Advanced pharmacological research in university labs
options.C: Highly specialized surgical assistance in sterile theaters
options.D: Private health insurance administration and billing

explanation: Before nursing became a structured profession, looking after the sick was mostly done by family members, volunteers, or religious groups just trying to keep patients comfortable. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: When a nurse makes sure a scared patient understands their surgery and rights before signing consent, what role is the nurse playing?
explanation: You are the patient's voice! As an advocate, you protect your patients' rights and make sure they are fully informed and comfortable with their care. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: When you teach a newly diagnosed diabetic patient how to give themselves insulin injections, which nursing role are you showing?
explanation: Spot on! Whenever you teach patients how to manage their health at home, you are stepping proudly into the educator role. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which option lists the four core concepts of the nursing metaparadigm?
explanation: Keep this close to your heart: Person, environment, health, and nursing are the four big pillars that build the foundation of our entire profession. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: Within nursing, how is 'health' best described?

options.A: A static biological condition that never changes throughout life
options.B: The exact moment a patient is discharged from the hospital ward
options.C: The total financial cost of medical treatments provided to a client
options.D: A dynamic state of complete well-being, not just absence of disease

explanation: Health isn't just 'not being sick in bed.' Nursing looks at health as a flowing, changing state of physical, mental, and social well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: What ethical principle means the nurse must always do good and act in the best interest of the patient?
explanation: Think of 'beneficence' as 'benevolent'—it's your daily professional duty to take positive steps to help and benefit your patients. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is accountability so important for every professional nurse?

options.A: It ensures that nurses receive higher salaries than other hospital staff
options.B: Accountability prevents nurses from working long night shifts
options.C: It allows nurses to override medical doctors during emergency surgeries
options.D: Nurses are legally and morally responsible for the direct consequences of their clinical actions

explanation: Being accountable means owning your clinical decisions and actions. When you care for a patient, you are responsible for the safe care you give them! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which official body regulates nursing training and practice here in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity

explanation: As a Nigerian nursing student, get very familiar with the NMCN! They set the rules, exams, and standards for our noble profession in the country. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the main goal of having a legal scope of nursing practice?

options.A: To eliminate the need for doctors in rural health centers
options.B: To reduce the salaries paid to junior nursing interns
options.C: To restrict the total number of students admitted into universities
options.D: To safeguard public health and ensure safe, competent care

explanation: Our scope of practice sets clear boundaries so the public is protected from quacks, ensuring that everyone who receives care gets safe and skilled treatment. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h7)
